nodes.name: Conventions on the base field and derived functors
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper we work over a field $\kk$, whose characteristic is assumed to be distinct from~2 and~3. In sections~\ref{section:preliminaries}, \ref{section:dp6-single} and~\ref{section:moduli-spaces} we assume that $\kk$ is algebraically closed, while in sections~\ref{section:families} and~\ref{section:special-families} we leave this assumption. For a scheme $X$ we denote by $\bD(X)$ the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X$, and unless something else is specified explicitly, this is what we mean by a derived category. All functors that we consider are derived --- for instance $\otimes$ stands for the derived tensor product, $f^*$ and~$f_*$ stand for the derived pullback and pushforward functors. If we want to consider the classical pullback or pushforward, we write $L_0f^*$ and $R^0f_*$ respectively (and similarly for other classical functors). We think of the Brauer group of a scheme as of the group of Morita-equivalence classes of Azumaya algebras on it. For a Brauer class $\beta$ on a scheme $X$ we denote by $\bD(X,\beta)$ the twisted bounded derived category of coherent sheaves. We refer to~\cite{huybrechts} for an introduction into derived categories, and to~\cite{icm2014} and references therein for an introduction into semiorthogonal decompositions.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Work over a field $\kk$ of characteristic $\ne 2,3$; $\bD(X)$ is the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves and all functors are derived.

nodes.name: Extension of the method to del Pezzo families of other degrees
nodes.statement: Of course, the approach used in this paper can be applied to del Pezzo families of other degree. In case of a single del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field one should analyze possible configurations of $(-2)$-curves on its weak del Pezzo resolution and find a semiorthogonal decomposition such that for any $(-2)$-curve $\Delta$ the sheaf $\cO_\Delta(-1)$ is contained in one of its components. Most probably, (weak del Pezzo analogues of) the three-block collections of Karpov and Nogin~\cite{karpov-nogin} should be used here. This approach definitely should work for del Pezzo surfaces of degrees $d \ge 5$, and we leave it to the readers to check the results it leads to.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: The same $(-2)$-curve/three-block strategy should work for del Pezzo families of degree $d \ge 5$.

nodes.name: Semiorthogonal decompositions for families of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $d \le 4$
nodes.statement: For $d \le 4$, however, the results of~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{auel2015semiorthogonal} show that an $S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition for a general flat family~$\cX \to S$ whose components are twisted derived categories of finite coverings of~$S$ does not exist. So, a new idea is needed to treat this case. We hope that the approach developed in~\cite{KKS} will be useful.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: For $d \le 4$ no decomposition into twisted derived categories of finite coverings of $S$ exists, so a new idea is needed.

nodes.name: sextic du Val del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement: A {\sf sextic du Val del Pezzo surface} is a normal integral projective surface $X$ over a field $\kk$ with at worst du Val singularities and ample anticanonical class such that $K_X^2 = 6$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
differentia: with at worst du Val singularities
nodes.definiendum: sextic du Val del Pezzo surface
nodes.genus: normal integral projective surface $X$ over a field $\kk$

nodes.name: Six configuration types of blowup centers and $(-2)$-curves on $\tX$
nodes.statement: By~\cite[Section~8.4.2]{dolgachev2012cag} there are six possibilities for configurations of the blowup centers and $(-2)$-curves on $\tX$ (see Table~\ref{table:dp6} below for a picture). \begin{description} \item[Type 0] Neither of $P_i$ lies on the exceptional divisor in $X_{i-1}$ and their images in $\P^2$ do not lie on a common line. Then $\tX$ contains no $(-2)$-curves and $X = \tX$ is smooth. \item[Type 1] Neither of $P_i$ lies on the exceptional divisor in $X_{i-1}$ but their images in $\P^2$ lie on a common line. Then $\tX$ contains a unique $(-2)$-curve (the strict transform $\Delta_{123}$ of that line) and~$X$ has one~$A_1$ singularity. \item[Type 2] The point $P_2$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$, the point $P_3$ is away from the exceptional divisors, and the line through $P_1$ in the direction of $P_2$ on $\P^2$ does not pass through the image of $P_3$. Then $\tX$ contains a unique $(-2)$-curve (the strict transform $\Delta_{12}$ of the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$) and $X$ has one $A_1$ singularity. \item[Type 3] The point $P_2$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$, the point $P_3$ is away from the exceptional divisors, but the line through $P_1$ in the direction of $P_2$ on $\P^2$ passes through the image of $P_3$. Then $\tX$ contains two disjoint $(-2)$-curves (the strict transforms $\Delta_{123}$ and $\Delta_{12}$ of the line on~$\P^2$ and of the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$, respectively) and $X$ has two $A_1$ singularities. \item[Type 4] The point $P_2$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$, the point $P_3$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_2 \to X_1$, and the strict transform $L_{12}$ of the line through $P_1$ in the direction of $P_2$ does not contain $P_3$. Then $\tX$ contains a 2-chain of $(-2)$-curves (the strict transforms $\Delta_{12}$ and $\Delta_{23}$ of the exceptional divisors of $X_1 \to X_0$ and $X_2 \to X_1$, respectively) and $X$ has one $A_2$ singularity. \item[Type 5] The point $P_2$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$, the point $P_3$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_2 \to X_1$, and the strict transform of the line through $P_1$ in the direction of $P_2$ contains $P_3$. Then $\tX$ contains a 2-chain of $(-2)$-curves and one more $(-2)$-curve disjoint from the chain (the strict transforms $\Delta_{123}$, $\Delta_{12}$ and $\Delta_{23}$ of the line and the exceptional divisors of~$X_1 \to X_0$ and $X_2 \to X_1$ respectively) and $X$ has one $A_2$ singularity and one $A_1$ singularity. \end{description}
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: There are exactly six types (0--5) of configurations, giving $X$ zero, one or two $A_1$/$A_2$ singularities.
assumptions: Let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be the minimal (in particular crepant) resolution of singularities of $X$.
conclusions: there are six possibilities for configurations of the blowup centers and $(-2)$-curves on $\tX$ (see Table~\ref{table:dp6} below for a picture). \begin{description} \item[Type 0] Neither of $P_i$ lies on the exceptional divisor in $X_{i-1}$ and their images in $\P^2$ do not lie on a common line. Then $\tX$ contains no $(-2)$-curves and $X = \tX$ is smooth. \item[Type 1] Neither of $P_i$ lies on the exceptional divisor in $X_{i-1}$ but their images in $\P^2$ lie on a common line. Then $\tX$ contains a unique $(-2)$-curve (the strict transform $\Delta_{123}$ of that line) and~$X$ has one~$A_1$ singularity. \item[Type 2] The point $P_2$ lies on the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$, the point $P_3$ is away from the exceptional divisors, and the line through $P_1$ in the direction of $P_2$ on $\P^2$ does not pass through the image of $P_3$. Then $\tX$ contains a unique $(-2)$-curve (the strict transform $\Delta_{12}$ of the exceptional divisor of $X_1 \to X_0$) and $X$ has one $A_1$ singularity.

nodes.name: Uniqueness and toricity of the sextic del Pezzo surface of each type
nodes.statement: In each of these types there is a unique (up to isomorphism) sextic del Pezzo surface. Moreover, the surfaces of types $0$, $2$, $3$, and $5$ are toric (in particular, the surface of type~5 is the weighted projective plane~$\P(1,2,3)$, see~\cite[Example~5.8]{kawamata2015multi} for an alternative description of its derived category). The surfaces of type~1 and~4 are not toric.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: Each type has a unique surface; types 0, 2, 3, 5 are toric and types 1, 4 are not.
conclusions: In each of these types there is a unique (up to isomorphism) sextic del Pezzo surface.

Moreover, the surfaces of types $0$, $2$, $3$, and $5$ are toric (in particular, the surface of type~5 is the weighted projective plane~$\P(1,2,3)$, see~\cite[Example~5.8]{kawamata2015multi} for an alternative description of its derived category). The surfaces of type~1 and~4 are not toric.

nodes.name: Picard group of the minimal resolution $\tX$
nodes.statement: We have $\Pic(\tX) \cong \ZZ\langle h, e_1,e_2,e_3 \rangle$, with $h^2 = 1$, $e_i^2 = -1$, $he_i = e_ie_j = 0$ for all $i \ne j$. Moreover, \begin{equation} K_\tX = -3h + e_1 + e_2 + e_3 = \pi^*K_X. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: $\Pic(\tX)$ is free on $h,e_1,e_2,e_3$ with the standard intersection form and $K_\tX=-3h+e_1+e_2+e_3=\pi^*K_X$.
assumptions: Let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be the minimal (in particular crepant) resolution of singularities of $X$.
conclusions: We have $\Pic(\tX) \cong \ZZ\langle h, e_1,e_2,e_3 \rangle$, with $h^2 = 1$, $e_i^2 = -1$, $he_i = e_ie_j = 0$ for all $i \ne j$.

nodes.name: Properties of $\pi^*$ and $\pi_*$ for a resolution of rational surface singularities
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a normal surface with rational singularities and let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its resolution. The functor $\pi^* \colon \bD^-(X) \to \bD^-(\tX)$ is fully faithful. The functor $\pi_* \colon \bD^-(\tX) \to \bD^-(X)$ is its right adjoint, it preserves boundedness, and there is an isomorphism of functors \begin{equation} \pi_* \circ \pi^* \cong \id. \end{equation} Moreover, \begin{equation*} \Ima \pi^* = {}^\perp\langle \cO_\Delta(-1) \rangle_{\Delta \in \bDelta} \qquand \Ker \pi_* = \langle \cO_\Delta(-1) \rangle^\oplus_{\Delta \in \bDelta}, \end{equation*} where $\langle - \rangle^\oplus$ denotes the minimal triangulated subcategory closed under infinite direct sums defined in $\bD^-$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: $\pi^*$ is fully faithful with right adjoint $\pi_*$, $\pi_*\pi^*\cong\id$, and $\Ker\pi_*$ is generated by the sheaves $\cO_\Delta(-1)$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a normal surface with rational singularities and let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its resolution.
conclusions: The functor $\pi^* \colon \bD^-(X) \to \bD^-(\tX)$ is fully faithful. The functor $\pi_* \colon \bD^-(\tX) \to \bD^-(X)$ is its right adjoint, it preserves boundedness

\Ima \pi^* = {}^\perp\langle \cO_\Delta(-1) \rangle_{\Delta \in \bDelta} \qquand \Ker \pi_* = \langle \cO_\Delta(-1) \rangle^\oplus_{\Delta \in \bDelta}, \end{equation*} where $\langle - \rangle^\oplus$ denotes the minimal triangulated subcategory closed under infinite direct sums defined in $\bD^-$.

nodes.name: Bridgeland's spectral sequence lemma
nodes.statement: Let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be a proper morphism with fibers of dimension at most~$1$. Let $\cF$ be a possibly unbounded complex of quasicoherent sheaves on $\tX$ and let $\cH^i(\cF)$ be its cohomology sheaf in degree $i$. The spectral sequence $R^i\pi_*(\cH^j(\cF)) \Rightarrow \cH^{i+j}(\pi_*(\cF))$ degenerates at the second page, and gives for each $i$ an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to R^1\pi_*\cH^{i-1}(\cF) \to \cH^i(\pi_*(\cF)) \to R^0\pi_*\cH^i(\cF) \to 0. \end{equation*} In particular, if $\cH^i(\pi_*(\cF)) = 0$ for $i \le p$ for some integer $p$, then $\pi_*(\cH^i(\cF)) = 0$ for $i \le p - 1$ and \begin{equation*} \pi_*\cF \cong \pi_*(\tau^{\ge p}\cF), \end{equation*} where $\tau$ stands for the truncation functor with respect to the canonical filtration.

nodes.statement_short: For a proper morphism with at most 1-dimensional fibers the spectral sequence $R^i\pi_*\cH^j \Rightarrow \cH^{i+j}\pi_*$ degenerates at $E_2$.

nodes.name: Essential surjectivity of $\pi_*$
nodes.statement: The functor $\pi_* \colon \bD(\tX) \to \bD(X)$ is essentially surjective.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
assumptions: Let $X$ be a normal surface with rational singularities and let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its resolution.
conclusions: The functor $\pi_* \colon \bD(\tX) \to \bD(X)$ is essentially surjective.

nodes.name: Grothendieck duality
nodes.statement: Let $f \colon X \to Y$ be a proper morphism. The {\sf Grothendieck duality} is a bifunctorial isomorphism \begin{equation} \RHom(f_*\cF,\cG) \cong \RHom(\cF,f^!\cG), \end{equation} where $f^!$ is the twisted pullback functor (if $\cG$ is perfect, $f^!\cG \cong \cG \otimes \omega^\bullet_{X/Y}$, where $\omega^\bullet_{X/Y} = f^!\cO_Y$ is the relative dualizing complex). In other words, the twisted pullback functor is right adjoint to the (derived) pushforward.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: The bifunctorial isomorphism $\RHom(f_*\cF,\cG)\cong\RHom(\cF,f^!\cG)$ making $f^!$ right adjoint to $f_*$.

nodes.name: Serre duality for Gorenstein schemes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a projective Gorenstein $\kk$-scheme of dimension $n$. If either $\cF$ or $\cG$ is a perfect complex, there is a natural Serre duality isomorphism \begin{equation*} \Ext^i(\cF,\cG)^\vee \cong \Ext^{n-i}(\cG,\cF \otimes \omega_X). \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: $\Ext^i(\cF,\cG)^\vee \cong \Ext^{n-i}(\cG,\cF\otimes\omega_X)$ on a projective Gorenstein $\kk$-scheme of dimension $n$.
nodes.origin_citation: classical Serre duality; consequence of Grothendieck duality
assumptions: Let $X$ be a projective Gorenstein $\kk$-scheme of dimension $n$.
If either $\cF$ or $\cG$ is a perfect complex
conclusions: there is a natural Serre duality isomorphism \begin{equation*} \Ext^i(\cF,\cG)^\vee \cong \Ext^{n-i}(\cG,\cF \otimes \omega_X).

nodes.name: The duality functor $\cF \mapsto \cF^\vee$
nodes.statement: Let us also discuss a contravariant duality functor or a projective $\kk$-scheme~$X$. It follows from sheafified Grothendieck duality that \begin{equation*} \RCHom(-,\omega^\bullet_{X/\kk}) \colon \bD(X)^{\mathrm{opp}} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \bD(X). \end{equation*} is an equivalence of categories. In case when the scheme $X$ is Gorenstein, the dualizing complex $\omega^\bullet_{X/\kk}$ is a shift of the canonical line bundle, $\omega^\bullet_{X/\kk} \cong \omega_X[\dim X]$, and it follows that the usual duality functor \begin{equation*} \cF \mapsto \cF^\vee := \RCHom(\cF,\cO_X) \cong \RCHom(\cF,\omega_X^\bullet) \otimes \omega_X^{-1}[-\dim X] \end{equation*} is also an equivalence of categories $\bD(X)^{\mathrm{opp}} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \bD(X)$.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries
nodes.statement_short: On a Gorenstein projective $X$, $\cF^\vee := \RCHom(\cF,\cO_X)$ is an anti-autoequivalence of $\bD(X)$.

nodes.name: Three-block semiorthogonal decomposition of $\bD(\tX)$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field $\kk$ and let~$\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its minimal resolution of singularities. There is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(\tX) = \langle \tcA_1, \tcA_2, \tcA_3 \rangle, \end{equation} whose components are generated by the following exceptional collections of line bundles \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \tcA_1 &= \langle \cO_\tX \rangle,\\ \tcA_2 &= \langle \cO_\tX(h - e_1), \cO_\tX(h - e_2), \cO_\tX(h - e_3) \rangle,\\ \tcA_3 &= \langle \cO_\tX(h), \cO_\tX(2h - e_1 - e_2 - e_3) \rangle. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\bD(\tX)$ splits into three blocks generated by exceptional line bundles $\cO_\tX$; $\cO_\tX(h-e_i)$; $\cO_\tX(h),\cO_\tX(2h-e_1-e_2-e_3)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Karpov & Nogin, Proposition 4.2(3); Auel & Bernardara, proof of Proposition 9.1
assumptions: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field $\kk$ and let~$\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its minimal resolution of singularities.
conclusions: There is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(\tX) = \langle \tcA_1, \tcA_2, \tcA_3 \rangle, \end{equation} whose components are generated by the following exceptional collections of line bundles \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \tcA_1 &= \langle \cO_\tX \rangle,\\ \tcA_2 &= \langle \cO_\tX(h - e_1), \cO_\tX(h - e_2), \cO_\tX(h - e_3) \rangle,\\ \tcA_3 &= \langle \cO_\tX(h), \cO_\tX(2h - e_1 - e_2 - e_3) \rangle.

nodes.name: Orthogonality inside the blocks $\tcA_i$ fails for singular $X$
nodes.statement: If $X$ is smooth (hence $\tX = X$) the exceptional line bundles in each of the components $\tcA_i$ of~\eqref{eq:tx-excol} are pairwise orthogonal. However, for singular $X$ this is no longer true.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The line bundles in each block are pairwise orthogonal exactly when $X$ is smooth.
conclusions: If $X$ is smooth (hence $\tX = X$) the exceptional line bundles in each of the components $\tcA_i$ of~\eqref{eq:tx-excol} are pairwise orthogonal.
However, for singular $X$ this is no longer true.

nodes.name: The dual decomposition of $\bD(\tX)$ is the right mutation-dual one
nodes.statement: The semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbtx-dual} is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:dbtx}, i.e., \begin{equation*} \tcA_1^\vee = \tcA_1, \qquad \tcA_2^\vee = \LL_{\tcA_1}(\tcA_2), \quad\text{and}\quad \tcA_3^\vee = \LL_{\tcA_1}(\LL_{\tcA_2}(\tcA_3)) = \tcA_3 \otimes \omega_\tX. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\tcA_1^\vee=\tcA_1$, $\tcA_2^\vee=\LL_{\tcA_1}(\tcA_2)$ and $\tcA_3^\vee=\tcA_3\otimes\omega_\tX$.
assumptions: the derived dualization functor $\cF \mapsto \cF^\vee$ provides an anti-autoequiva\-lence of~$\bD(\tX)$.
Below we denote by $\LL_\cA$ the left mutation functor through an admissible subcategory $\cA$.
conclusions: The semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbtx-dual} is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:dbtx}, i.e., \begin{equation*} \tcA_1^\vee = \tcA_1, \qquad \tcA_2^\vee = \LL_{\tcA_1}(\tcA_2), \quad\text{and}\quad \tcA_3^\vee = \LL_{\tcA_1}(\LL_{\tcA_2}(\tcA_3)) = \tcA_3 \otimes \omega_\tX.

nodes.name: The components $\tcA_i$ as derived categories of Auslander algebras
nodes.statement: The components $\tcA_i$ of~\eqref{eq:dbtx} are equivalent to products of derived categories of Auslander algebras as indicated in the next table: \begin{equation*}\def\arraystretch{1.7} \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Type of $X$} & \tcA_1 & \tcA_2 & \tcA_3 \\ \hline 0 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 1 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \\ \hline 2 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 3 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \\ \hline 4 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_3) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 5 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_3) & \bD(\tR_2) \\ \hline \end{array} \end{equation*} This equivalence takes the exceptional line bundles in~\eqref{eq:tx-excol} to the standard exceptional modules over the corresponding Auslander algebra.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: Each $\tcA_i$ is a product of $\bD(\kk)$'s and $\bD(\tR_m)$'s determined by the type of $X$, matching exceptional line bundles with standard exceptional modules.
assumptions: For $m = 2$ and $m = 3$ we denote by $\tR_m$ the Auslander algebra defined by~\eqref{eq:trm}, and refer to Appendix~\ref{appendix:auslander} for its basic properties,
conclusions: The components $\tcA_i$ of~\eqref{eq:dbtx} are equivalent to products of derived categories of Auslander algebras as indicated in the next table: \begin{equation*}\def\arraystretch{1.7} \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Type of $X$} & \tcA_1 & \tcA_2 & \tcA_3 \\ \hline 0 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 1 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \\ \hline 2 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 3 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_2) \\ \hline 4 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_3) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 5 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\tR_3) & \bD(\tR_2) \\ \hline \end{array} \end{equation*} This equivalence takes the exceptional line bundles in~\eqref{eq:tx-excol} to the standard exceptional modules over the corresponding Auslander algebra.

nodes.name: Realization of the nontrivial morphisms between the exceptional line bundles
nodes.statement: The nontrivial morphisms between the line bundles $\cO_\tX(h-e_1)$, $\cO_\tX(h-e_2)$, and $\cO_\tX(h-e_3)$ when exist are realized by exact sequences~\eqref{eq:e12} and~\eqref{eq:e23}. Analogously, the nontrivial morphism between the line bundles $\cO_\tX(h)$ and $\cO_\tX(2h - e_1 - e_2 - e_3)$ is realized by the exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to \cO_\tX(h) \xrightarrow{\ \Delta_{123}\ } \cO_\tX(2h - e_1 - e_2 - e_3) \to \cO_{\Delta_{123}}(-1) \to 0. \end{equation} This shows that each category $\tcA_i$ is a product of categories of the form described in~\cite[Theorem~2.5]{hille2017tilting}, and in fact, the Auslander algebras $\tR_m$ appearing in Proposition~\ref{proposition:tcai-auslander}, are nothing but the particular forms of the algebras from \emph{loc.\ cit.}, cf.~\cite[\S3.2]{hille2017tilting}.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The nonzero maps between the generating line bundles come from the exact sequences attached to the $(-2)$-curves, so each $\tcA_i$ has the Hille--Ploog form.
conclusions: The nontrivial morphisms between the line bundles $\cO_\tX(h-e_1)$, $\cO_\tX(h-e_2)$, and $\cO_\tX(h-e_3)$ when exist are realized by exact sequences~\eqref{eq:e12} and~\eqref{eq:e23}.
This shows that each category $\tcA_i$ is a product of categories of the form described in~\cite[Theorem~2.5]{hille2017tilting},

nodes.name: Sheaves $\cO_\Delta(-1)$ correspond to simple modules
nodes.statement: Comparing exact sequences~\eqref{eq:resolution-simple} of standard exceptional modules over an Auslander algebra with the exact sequences~\eqref{eq:e12}, \eqref{eq:e23} and~\eqref{eq:e123}, and taking into account that the equivalence of Proposition~\ref{proposition:tcai-auslander} takes the exceptional line bundles generating $\tcA_i$ to the standard exceptional modules over the corresponding Auslander algebras, we conclude that the sheaves~$\cO_\Delta(-1)$ go to the corresponding simple modules. For instance, for a surface of type 5, when we have the maximal number of $(-2)$-curves on $\tX$, and when $\tcA_2 \cong \bD(\tR_3)$, $\tcA_3 \cong \bD(\tR_2)$, the sheaves $\cO_{\Delta_{12}}(-1)$ and~$\cO_{\Delta_{23}}(-1)$ go to $S_1$ and $S_2$ in $\bD(\tR_3)$, and the sheaf $\cO_{\Delta_{123}}(-1)$ goes to $S_1$ in $\bD(\tR_2)$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: Under the equivalence $\tcA_i \cong \bD(\tR_m)$ the sheaves $\cO_\Delta(-1)$ go to the simple modules $S_j$.

nodes.name: Semiorthogonal decomposition of $\bD(X)$ for a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field~$\kk$, and let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its minimal resolution of singularities. Then there is a unique semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(X) = \langle \cA_1, \cA_2, \cA_3 \rangle, \end{equation} such that $\pi_*(\tcA_i) = \cA_i$ and $\pi^*(\cA_i \cap \bD^\perf(X)) \subset \tcA_i$, where $\tcA_i$ are the components of~\eqref{eq:dbtx}. The components~$\cA_i$ are admissible with projection functors of finite cohomological amplitude, and are equivalent to products of derived categories of finite-dimensional algebras as indicated in the next table: \begin{equation*}\def\arraystretch{1.2} \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Type of $X$} & \cA_1 & \cA_2 & \cA_3 \\ \hline 0 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 1 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^2) \\ \hline 2 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^2) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 3 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^2) \times \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^2) \\ \hline 4 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^3) & \bD(\kk) \times \bD(\kk) \\ \hline 5 & \bD(\kk) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^3) & \bD(\kk[t]/t^2) \\ \hline \end{array} \end{equation*} The categories $\cA_i^\perf := \cA_i \cap \bD^\perf(X)$ form a semiorthogonal decomposition of the perfect category \begin{equation*} \bD^\perf(X) = \langle \cA_1^\perf, \cA_2^\perf, \cA_3^\perf \rangle. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\bD(X)=\langle\cA_1,\cA_2,\cA_3\rangle$ with admissible components equivalent to products of $\bD(\kk[t]/t^m)$, compatible with $\pi_*$ and $\pi^*$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field~$\kk$, and let $\pi \colon \tX \to X$ be its minimal resolution of singularities.
conclusions: Then there is a unique semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(X) = \langle \cA_1, \cA_2, \cA_3 \rangle, \end{equation} such that $\pi_*(\tcA_i) = \cA_i$ and $\pi^*(\cA_i \cap \bD^\perf(X)) \subset \tcA_i$, where $\tcA_i$ are the components of~

The components~$\cA_i$ are admissible with projection functors of finite cohomological amplitude, and are equivalent to products of derived categories of finite-dimensional algebras as indicated in the next table:

The categories $\cA_i^\perf := \cA_i \cap \bD^\perf(X)$ form a semiorthogonal decomposition of the perfect category \begin{equation*} \bD^\perf(X) = \langle \cA_1^\perf, \cA_2^\perf, \cA_3^\perf \rangle.

nodes.name: Intersections of $\tcA_i^-$ with $\Ker\pi_*$
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation*} \tcA_1^- \cap \Ker \pi_* = 0, \qquad \tcA_2^- \cap \Ker \pi_* = \langle \cO_{\Delta}(-1) \rangle^\oplus_{\Delta \in \bDelta_2}, \quand \tcA_3^- \cap \Ker \pi_* = \langle \cO_{\Delta}(-1) \rangle^\oplus_{\Delta \in \bDelta_3}. \end{equation*} Moreover, for any $\cF \in \Ker\pi_* \subset \bD^-(\tX)$ there is a canonical direct sum decomposition \begin{equation*} \cF = \cF_2 \oplus \cF_3 \end{equation*} with $\cF_j \in \tcA_j^- \cap \Ker \pi_*$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\Ker\pi_*$ meets $\tcA_1^-$ trivially and splits over $\tcA_2^-,\tcA_3^-$ according to the two families of $(-2)$-curves.
assumptions: Recall that $\bDelta$ denotes the set of all $(-2)$-curves defined on $\tX$. We denote by $\bDelta_2 \subset \bDelta$ the subset formed by those of the curves $\Delta_{12}$ and $\Delta_{23}$ that are defined on $\tX$ and by $\bDelta_3 \subset \bDelta$ its complement.
conclusions: We have \begin{equation*} \tcA_1^- \cap \Ker \pi_* = 0, \qquad \tcA_2^- \cap \Ker \pi_* = \langle \cO_{\Delta}(-1) \rangle^\oplus_{\Delta \in \bDelta_2}, \quand \tcA_3^- \cap \Ker \pi_* = \langle \cO_{\Delta}(-1) \rangle^\oplus_{\Delta \in \bDelta_3}. \end{equation*} Moreover, for any $\cF \in \Ker\pi_* \subset \bD^-(\tX)$ there is a canonical direct sum decomposition \begin{equation*} \cF = \cF_2 \oplus \cF_3 \end{equation*} with $\cF_j \in \tcA_j^- \cap \Ker \pi_*$.

nodes.name: Orthogonality of $\tcA_i^-$ against $\tcA_j^- \cap \Ker\pi_*$
nodes.statement: We have $\Hom(\tcA_i^-,\tcA_j^- \cap \Ker \pi_*) = 0$ for any $i \ne j$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
assumptions: \bD^-(\tX) = \langle \tcA_1^-, \tcA_2^-, \tcA_3^- \rangle.
conclusions: We have $\Hom(\tcA_i^-,\tcA_j^- \cap \Ker \pi_*) = 0$ for any $i \ne j$.

nodes.name: Induced semiorthogonal decomposition of $\bD^-(X)$
nodes.statement: The subcategories $\cA_i^- = \{ \cF \in \bD^-(X) \mid \pi^*(\cF) \in \tcA_i^- \} \subset \bD^-(X)$ form a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} \bD^-(X) = \langle \cA_1^-, \cA_2^-, \cA_3^- \rangle \end{equation*} with projection functors given by \begin{equation} \alpha_i = \pi_* \circ \tilde\alpha_i \circ \pi^*. \end{equation} Moreover, we have \begin{equation} \pi_*(\tcA_i^-) = \cA_i^-. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The preimages $\cA_i^-$ of $\tcA_i^-$ under $\pi^*$ decompose $\bD^-(X)$, with projections $\alpha_i = \pi_*\tilde\alpha_i\pi^*$.
assumptions: Denote by $\tilde\alpha_i$ the projection functors of the decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbtx-}.
conclusions: The subcategories $\cA_i^- = \{ \cF \in \bD^-(X) \mid \pi^*(\cF) \in \tcA_i^- \} \subset \bD^-(X)$ form a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} \bD^-(X) = \langle \cA_1^-, \cA_2^-, \cA_3^- \rangle \end{equation*} with projection functors given by \begin{equation} \alpha_i = \pi_* \circ \tilde\alpha_i \circ \pi^*. \end{equation} Moreover, we have \begin{equation} \pi_*(\tcA_i^-) = \cA_i^-.

nodes.name: Semiorthogonal decomposition of the bounded category $\bD(X)$
nodes.statement: The subcategories \begin{equation*} \cA_i := \cA_i^- \cap \bD(X) = \{ \cF \in \bD(X) \mid \pi^*(\cF) \in \tcA_i^- \} \subset \bD(X) \end{equation*} provide a semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx}. Its projection functors $\alpha_i$ are given by~\eqref{eq:alpha}; they preserve boundedness and have finite cohomological amplitude. Finally, $\cA_i = \pi_*(\tcA_i)$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The bounded parts $\cA_i$ give the decomposition, their projections preserve boundedness and $\cA_i = \pi_*(\tcA_i)$.
assumptions: The subcategories $\cA_i^- = \{ \cF \in \bD^-(X) \mid \pi^*(\cF) \in \tcA_i^- \} \subset \bD^-(X)$ form a semiorthogonal decomposition
conclusions: The subcategories \begin{equation*} \cA_i := \cA_i^- \cap \bD(X) = \{ \cF \in \bD(X) \mid \pi^*(\cF) \in \tcA_i^- \} \subset \bD(X) \end{equation*} provide a semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx}. Its projection functors $\alpha_i$ are given by~\eqref{eq:alpha}; they preserve boundedness and have finite cohomological amplitude. Finally, $\cA_i = \pi_*(\tcA_i)$.

nodes.name: The functor $\gamma = \pi_*\tilde\gamma\pi_m^*$ is fully faithful
nodes.statement: The functor \begin{equation} \gamma := \pi_* \circ \tilde\gamma \circ \pi_m^* \colon \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \to \bD^-(X). \end{equation} is fully faithful and preserves boundedness. Moreover, the diagrams \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix@C=5em{ \bD^-(\tR_m) \ar[r]^-{\tilde\gamma} \ar[d]_{\pi_{m*}} & \bD^-(\tX) \ar[d]^{\pi_{*}} \\ \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \ar[r]^{\gamma} & \bD^-(X) }} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \vcenter{\xymatrix@C=5em{ \bD^-(\tR_m) \ar[r]^-{\tilde\gamma} & \bD^-(\tX) \\ \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \ar[r]^{\gamma} \ar[u]^{\pi_m^{*}} & \bD^-(X) \ar[u]_{\pi^{*}} }} \end{equation} are both commutative.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\gamma$ embeds $\bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m)$ into $\bD^-(X)$, preserves boundedness and commutes with the two resolution squares.
assumptions: Take one of these and denote by $\tilde\gamma \colon \bD(\tR_m) \to \bD(\tX)$ its embedding functor. Let \begin{equation*} \pi_{m*} \colon \bD^-(\tR_m) \to \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \pi_m^* \colon \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \to \bD^-(\tR_m) \end{equation*} be the functors described in Appendix~\ref{appendix:auslander}, see equation~\eqref{eq:pms}. Note that $\pi_m^*$ is left adjoint to~$\pi_{m*}$.
conclusions: The functor \begin{equation} \gamma := \pi_* \circ \tilde\gamma \circ \pi_m^* \colon \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \to \bD^-(X). \end{equation} is fully faithful and preserves boundedness. Moreover, the diagrams \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix@C=5em{ \bD^-(\tR_m) \ar[r]^-{\tilde\gamma} \ar[d]_{\pi_{m*}} & \bD^-(\tX) \ar[d]^{\pi_{*}} \\ \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \ar[r]^{\gamma} & \bD^-(X) }} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \vcenter{\xymatrix@C=5em{ \bD^-(\tR_m) \ar[r]^-{\tilde\gamma} & \bD^-(\tX) \\ \bD^-(\kk[t]/t^m) \ar[r]^{\gamma} \ar[u]^{\pi_m^{*}} & \bD^-(X) \ar[u]_{\pi^{*}} }} \end{equation} are both commutative.

nodes.name: Completely orthogonal decomposition of $\cA_i$
nodes.statement: The fully faithful functors $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_s$ induce a completely orthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} \cA_i = \bD(\kk[t]/t^{m_1}) \times \dots \times \bD(\kk[t]/t^{m_s}). \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The embeddings $\gamma_j$ decompose $\cA_i$ as a product of the categories $\bD(\kk[t]/t^{m_j})$.
assumptions: Let $\tcA_i = \bD(\tR_{m_1}) \times \dots \times \bD(\tR_{m_s})$ be the corresponding component of~\eqref{eq:dbtx}. Let $\tilde\gamma_j \colon \bD(\tR_{m_j}) \to \bD(\tX)$ be the corresponding embedding functors and let $\gamma_j \colon \bD(\kk[t]/t^{m_j}) \to \bD(X)$ be the embeddings constructed in Proposition~\ref{proposition:gamma}.
conclusions: The fully faithful functors $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_s$ induce a completely orthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} \cA_i = \bD(\kk[t]/t^{m_1}) \times \dots \times \bD(\kk[t]/t^{m_s}).

nodes.name: Admissibility of the components $\cA_i$
nodes.statement: The subcategories $\cA_i \subset \bD(X)$ in~\eqref{eq:dbx} are admissible.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
conclusions: The subcategories $\cA_i \subset \bD(X)$ in~\eqref{eq:dbx} are admissible.

nodes.name: Geometric form: $\bD(X)=\langle\bD(Z_1),\bD(Z_2),\bD(Z_3)\rangle$
nodes.statement: For every sextic du Val del Pezzo surface $X$ over an algebraically closed field $\kk$ there are zero-dimensional Gorenstein schemes $Z_1$, $Z_2$, $Z_3$ of lengths $1$, $3$, and $2$ respectively, such that $\cA_i \cong \bD(Z_i)$ and \begin{equation} \bD(X) = \langle \bD(Z_1), \bD(Z_2), \bD(Z_3) \rangle. \end{equation} The scheme structure of $Z_i$ depends on the type of $X$ as follows: \begin{equation*}\def\arraystretch{1.2} \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Type of $X$} & Z_1 & Z_2 & Z_3 \\ \hline 0 & \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) \\ \hline 1 & \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^2) \\ \hline 2 & \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^2) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) \\ \hline 3 & \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^2) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^2) \\ \hline 4 & \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^3) & \Spec(\kk) \sqcup \Spec(\kk) \\ \hline 5 & \Spec(\kk) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^3) & \Spec(\kk[t]/t^2) \\ \hline \end{array} \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The three components are derived categories of zero-dimensional Gorenstein schemes $Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$ of lengths $1,3,2$ depending on the type of $X$.
assumptions: For every sextic du Val del Pezzo surface $X$ over an algebraically closed field $\kk$
conclusions: there are zero-dimensional Gorenstein schemes $Z_1$, $Z_2$, $Z_3$ of lengths $1$, $3$, and $2$ respectively, such that $\cA_i \cong \bD(Z_i)$ and \begin{equation} \bD(X) = \langle \bD(Z_1), \bD(Z_2), \bD(Z_3) \rangle. \end{equation} The scheme structure of $Z_i$ depends on the type of $X$ as follows:

nodes.name: Dual semiorthogonal decomposition of $\bD(X)$
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a sextic del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(X) = \langle \cA_3^\vee, \cA_2^\vee, \cA_1^\vee \rangle, \end{equation} where \begin{equation*} \cA_i^\vee := \{ \cF \in \bD(X) \mid \cF^\vee \in \cA_i \} \cong \bD(Z_i), \end{equation*} and $\cA_i$ are the components of~\eqref{eq:dbx}. Moreover, this semiorthogonal decomposition is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:dbx}, i.e., $\cA_1^\vee = \cA_1$, $\cA_2^\vee = \LL_{\cA_1}(\cA_2)$ and $\cA_3^\vee = \LL_{\cA_1}(\LL_{\cA_2}(\cA_3))$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: Dualizing gives $\bD(X)=\langle\cA_3^\vee,\cA_2^\vee,\cA_1^\vee\rangle$, the right mutation-dual of the original decomposition.
assumptions: If $X$ is a sextic del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field
conclusions: there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(X) = \langle \cA_3^\vee, \cA_2^\vee, \cA_1^\vee \rangle, \end{equation} where \begin{equation*} \cA_i^\vee := \{ \cF \in \bD(X) \mid \cF^\vee \in \cA_i \} \cong \bD(Z_i), \end{equation*} and $\cA_i$ are the components of~\eqref{eq:dbx}. Moreover, this semiorthogonal decomposition is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:dbx}, i.e., $\cA_1^\vee = \cA_1$, $\cA_2^\vee = \LL_{\cA_1}(\cA_2)$ and $\cA_3^\vee = \LL_{\cA_1}(\LL_{\cA_2}(\cA_3))$.

nodes.name: Sheaves on $Y \times \Spec(\kk[t]/t^m)$ and a flatness criterion
nodes.statement: Let $Z = \Spec(\kk[t]/t^m)$. For any scheme $Y$ we have an equivalence \begin{equation*} \coh(Y \times Z) \cong \coh(Y,\cO_Y[t]/t^m), \end{equation*} where the right hand side is the category of coherent sheaves $\cF$ on $Y$ with an operator $t \colon \cF \to \cF$ such that $t^m = 0$. An object $(\cF,t) \in \coh(Y,\cO_Y[t]/t^m)$ considered as a sheaf on $Y \times Z$ is flat over $Z$ if and only if all the maps in the next chain of epimorphisms \begin{equation} \xymatrix@1{\cF/(t\cF) \ar@{->>}[r]^-t & (t\cF)/(t^2\cF) \ar@{->>}[r]^-t & \ \dots\ \ar@{->>}[r]^-t & (t^{m-1}\cF)/(t^m\cF)} \end{equation} are isomorphisms.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: Coherent sheaves on $Y\times Z$ are sheaves with a nilpotent operator $t$, and flatness over $Z$ means the induced epimorphisms between the $t$-quotients are isomorphisms.
assumptions: Let $Z = \Spec(\kk[t]/t^m)$.
For any scheme $Y$
conclusions: we have an equivalence \begin{equation*} \coh(Y \times Z) \cong \coh(Y,\cO_Y[t]/t^m), \end{equation*} where the right hand side is the category of coherent sheaves $\cF$ on $Y$ with an operator $t \colon \cF \to \cF$ such that $t^m = 0$.

An object $(\cF,t) \in \coh(Y,\cO_Y[t]/t^m)$ considered as a sheaf on $Y \times Z$ is flat over $Z$ if and only if all the maps in the next chain of epimorphisms \begin{equation} \xymatrix@1{\cF/(t\cF) \ar@{->>}[r]^-t & (t\cF)/(t^2\cF) \ar@{->>}[r]^-t & \ \dots\ \ar@{->>}[r]^-t & (t^{m-1}\cF)/(t^m\cF)} \end{equation} are isomorphisms.

nodes.name: The sheaves $\cE_z$ attached to closed points of $Z_d$
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: Each $\cE_z = \gamma_{Z_d}(\cO_z)$ is the pushforward of an explicit line bundle on $\tX$; it is globally generated with $\dim H^0 = d$ and no higher cohomology.
assumptions: In what follows for a connected component $Z$ of $Z_d$ we denote by $\gamma_Z$ the embedding functor (constructed in Proposition~\ref{proposition:gamma}) \begin{equation*} \gamma_Z \colon \bD(Z) \hookrightarrow \bD(X),
conclusions: In all these cases, $\cE_z$ is a globally generated sheaf, and if $z \in Z_d$ then \begin{equation*} \dim H^0(X,\cE_z) = d \qquand H^{i}(X,\cE_z) = 0 \quad\text{for $i \ne 0$}.

nodes.name: $\fE_Z$ and $\tfE_Z$ are vector bundles of rank $\ell(Z)$
nodes.statement: Both $\fE_Z$ and $\tfE_Z$ are vector bundles of rank~$\ell(Z)$ on~$X$ and~$\tX$ respectively, and \begin{equation} \fE_Z \cong \pi_*(\tfE_Z). \end{equation} Moreover, $\fE_Z$ is an iterated extension of the sheaf $\cE_z$, where $z$ is the closed point of~$Z$. In particular, the bundle $\fE_Z$ is globally generated with $\dim H^0(X,\fE_Z) = d\ell(Z)$ and $H^i(X,\fE_Z) = 0$ for $i \ne 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: The images of the structure sheaves of the components of $Z_d$ are globally generated vector bundles of rank $\ell(Z)$ with $\dim H^0 = d\ell(Z)$.
assumptions: Next we determine the images \begin{equation} \fE_Z := \gamma_Z(\cO_Z) \in \bD(X) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \tfE_Z := \pi^*(\fE_Z) \in \bD(\tX) \end{equation} of the structure sheaves of connected components of~$Z_d$. We denote by~$\ell(Z)$ the length of~$Z$.
conclusions: Both $\fE_Z$ and $\tfE_Z$ are vector bundles of rank~$\ell(Z)$ on~$X$ and~$\tX$ respectively, and \begin{equation} \fE_Z \cong \pi_*(\tfE_Z). \end{equation} Moreover, $\fE_Z$ is an iterated extension of the sheaf $\cE_z$, where $z$ is the closed point of~$Z$. In particular, the bundle $\fE_Z$ is globally generated with $\dim H^0(X,\fE_Z) = d\ell(Z)$ and $H^i(X,\fE_Z) = 0$ for $i \ne 0$.

nodes.name: The equivalences $\bD(Z_d)\cong\cA_d$ as Fourier--Mukai functors
nodes.statement: For each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ there is a sheaf \begin{equation*} \cE_{Z_d} \in \coh(X \times Z_d), \end{equation*} flat over $Z_d$, such that $p_{X*}\cE_{Z_d} \cong \fE_{Z_d}$, and the equivalence $\gamma_{Z_d} \colon \bD(Z_d) \to \cA_d \subset \bD(X)$ of Corollary~\textup{\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}} can be written as \begin{equation*} \gamma_{Z_d} \cong \Phi_{\cE_{Z_d}} \colon \bD(Z_d) \to \bD(X), \end{equation*} where $\Phi_{\cE_{Z_d}}$ is the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $\cE_{Z_d}$. Moreover, the equivalence \mbox{$\bD(Z_d) \cong \cA_d^\vee \subset \bD(X)$} of Proposition~\textup{\ref{proposition:dbx-dual}} is given by the Fourier--Mukai functor $\Phi_{\cE_{Z_d}^\vee}$ with kernel $\cE_{Z_d}^\vee$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: There is a sheaf $\cE_{Z_d}$ on $X\times Z_d$, flat over $Z_d$, whose Fourier--Mukai functor realizes $\gamma_{Z_d}$; its dual realizes the dual decomposition.
assumptions: By Proposition~\ref{proposition:e-z-big} these are globally generated vector bundles on $X$ of ranks $1$, $3$, and $2$ respectively. We denote by~\mbox{$p_X \colon X \times Z_d \to X$} the natural projection.
conclusions: For each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ there is a sheaf \begin{equation*} \cE_{Z_d} \in \coh(X \times Z_d), \end{equation*} flat over $Z_d$, such that $p_{X*}\cE_{Z_d} \cong \fE_{Z_d}$, and the equivalence $\gamma_{Z_d} \colon \bD(Z_d) \to \cA_d \subset \bD(X)$ of Corollary~\textup{\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}} can be written as \begin{equation*} \gamma_{Z_d} \cong \Phi_{\cE_{Z_d}} \colon \bD(Z_d) \to \bD(X), \end{equation*} where $\Phi_{\cE_{Z_d}}$ is the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $\cE_{Z_d}$. Moreover, the equivalence \mbox{$\bD(Z_d) \cong \cA_d^\vee \subset \bD(X)$} of Proposition~\textup{\ref{proposition:dbx-dual}} is given by the Fourier--Mukai functor $\Phi_{\cE_{Z_d}^\vee}$ with kernel $\cE_{Z_d}^\vee$.

nodes.name: $\cA_2$ and $\cA_3$ as orthogonals of $\cO_X$, $\fE_{Z_2}$, $\fE_{Z_3}$
nodes.statement: The components $\cA_2$ and $\cA_3$ of $\bD(X)$ are compactly generated by the bundles $\fE_{Z_2}$ and~$\fE_{Z_3}$ respectively. In particular, we have $\cA_2 = {}^\perp \cO_X \cap \fE_{Z_3}^\perp$ and $\cA_3 = {}^\perp \cO_X \cap {}^\perp\fE_{Z_2}$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\cA_2$ and $\cA_3$ are compactly generated by $\fE_{Z_2}$ and $\fE_{Z_3}$ and are cut out by orthogonality conditions.
conclusions: The components $\cA_2$ and $\cA_3$ of $\bD(X)$ are compactly generated by the bundles $\fE_{Z_2}$ and~$\fE_{Z_3}$ respectively. In particular, we have $\cA_2 = {}^\perp \cO_X \cap \fE_{Z_3}^\perp$ and $\cA_3 = {}^\perp \cO_X \cap {}^\perp\fE_{Z_2}$.

nodes.name: Euler characteristics against $\fE_{Z_2}$ and $\fE_{Z_3}$
nodes.statement: For any $\cF \in \bD(X)$ we have \begin{alignat*}{2} \chi(\fE_{Z_2},\cF) &= 2 &&\chi(\cO_X,\cF) + \chi(\cO_X,\cF(K_X)) - 3r(\cF),\\ \chi(\fE_{Z_3},\cF) &= &&\chi(\cO_X,\cF) + \chi(\cO_X,\cF(K_X)) - 2r(\cF). \end{alignat*}
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\chi(\fE_{Z_d},\cF)$ is expressed through $\chi(\cO_X,\cF)$, $\chi(\cO_X,\cF(K_X))$ and the rank $r(\cF)$.
assumptions: For any $\cF \in \bD(X)$
conclusions: \chi(\fE_{Z_2},\cF) &= 2 &&\chi(\cO_X,\cF) + \chi(\cO_X,\cF(K_X)) - 3r(\cF),\\ \chi(\fE_{Z_3},\cF) &= &&\chi(\cO_X,\cF) + \chi(\cO_X,\cF(K_X)) - 2r(\cF).

nodes.name: Pushforwards of the Fourier--Mukai kernels are vector bundles
nodes.statement: The pushforwards $p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}$ and $p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}$ are vector bundles on $Z_2$ and $Z_3$ of rank $2$ and $3$ respectively. Similarly, the pushforward $p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*\cE_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle on $Z_2 \times Z_3$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}$, $p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}$ are bundles of ranks $2,3$, and the mixed pushforward is a line bundle on $Z_2\times Z_3$.
assumptions: Denote by $p_2 \colon X \times Z_2 \to Z_2$, $p_3 \colon X \times Z_3 \to Z_3$, and $p_{23} \colon X \times Z_2 \times Z_3 \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the projections. Similarly, consider the projections $p_{X2} \colon X \times Z_2 \times Z_3 \to X \times Z_2$ and $p_{X3} \colon X \times Z_2 \times Z_3 \to X \times Z_3$.
conclusions: The pushforwards $p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}$ and $p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}$ are vector bundles on $Z_2$ and $Z_3$ of rank $2$ and $3$ respectively. Similarly, the pushforward $p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*\cE_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle on $Z_2 \times Z_3$.

nodes.name: Gluing bimodules between the components
nodes.statement: The above lemma can be interpreted as a computation of the gluing bimodules (cf.~\cite[Section~2.2]{kuznetsov2015categorical}) between the components of~\eqref{eq:dbx}. It says that $\bD(X)$ is the gluing of $\bD(\kk)$, $\bD(Z_2)$, and $\bD(Z_3)$ with the gluing bimodules being $\kk[Z_2]^{\oplus 2}$, $\kk[Z_2 \times Z_3]$, and $\kk[Z_3]^{\oplus 3}$.
nodes.section: 3 Derived category of a single sextic del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement_short: $\bD(X)$ is the gluing of $\bD(\kk),\bD(Z_2),\bD(Z_3)$ with explicit gluing bimodules.

nodes.name: Hilbert polynomial $h_\cF$ with respect to $-K_X$
nodes.statement: For a sheaf $\cF$ on $X$ we denote by \begin{equation*} h_\cF(t) := \chi(\cF(-tK_X)) \in \ZZ[t], \end{equation*} the Hilbert polynomial of $\cF$ with respect to the anticanonical polarization of $X$. This is a quadratic polynomial with the leading coefficient equal to $r(\cF)\cdot K_X^2/2 = 3r(\cF)$. Note that \begin{equation} h_{\cO_X}(t) = 3t(t+1) + 1. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: $h_\cF(t)=\chi(\cF(-tK_X))$, a quadratic polynomial with leading coefficient $3r(\cF)$.

nodes.name: The polynomials $h_d(t) = (3t+d)(t+1)$
nodes.statement: For each $d \in \ZZ$ we consider the polynomial \begin{equation} h_d(t) := (3t + d)(t+1) \in \ZZ[t]. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation

nodes.name: Ordering of the polynomials $h_d$ and $h_{\cO_X}$
nodes.statement: An elementary verification shows \begin{equation} h_4(t) > h_3(t) > h_2(t) > h_{\cO_X}(t) > h_4(t-1) > h_3(t-1) > h_2(t-1) \qquad\text{for all $t \gg 0$.} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: For $t \gg 0$ the polynomials $h_4,h_3,h_2,h_{\cO_X}$ and their shifts are strictly ordered.
conclusions: An elementary verification shows \begin{equation} h_4(t) > h_3(t) > h_2(t) > h_{\cO_X}(t) > h_4(t-1) > h_3(t-1) > h_2(t-1) \qquad\text{for all $t \gg 0$.

nodes.name: Semistability = stability = torsion-freeness for Hilbert polynomial $h_d$
nodes.statement: A sheaf $\cF$ on $X$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ is Gieseker semistable if and only if it is Gieseker stable and if and only if it is torsion-free.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
assumptions: A sheaf $\cF$ on $X$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$
conclusions: is Gieseker semistable if and only if it is Gieseker stable and if and only if it is torsion-free.

nodes.name: Stability and Hilbert polynomials of $\cE_z$, $\cE_z^\vee$ and $\fE_{Z_d}$
nodes.statement: Let $d \in \{2, 3\}$. For any closed point $z \in Z_d$ the sheaf $\cE_z$ is stable with $h_{\cE_z}(t) = h_d(t)$. Its derived dual~$\cE_z^\vee$ is a stable sheaf with $h_{\cE_z^\vee}(t) = h_d(-t-1) = h_{6-d}(t-1)$. Furthermore, the sheaf $\fE_{Z_d}$ is semistable with $h_{\fE_{Z_d}} = \ell(Z_d)h_d$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: $\cE_z$ is stable with $h_{\cE_z}=h_d$, its dual is stable with $h_d(-t-1)$, and $\fE_{Z_d}$ is semistable.
assumptions: For any closed point $z \in Z_d$
conclusions: the sheaf $\cE_z$ is stable with $h_{\cE_z}(t) = h_d(t)$. Its derived dual~$\cE_z^\vee$ is a stable sheaf with $h_{\cE_z^\vee}(t) = h_d(-t-1) = h_{6-d}(t-1)$. Furthermore, the sheaf $\fE_{Z_d}$ is semistable with $h_{\fE_{Z_d}} = \ell(Z_d)h_d$.

nodes.name: The moduli space $\cM_d(X)$ of semistable sheaves
nodes.statement: Denote by \begin{equation} \cM_d(X) := \cM_{X,-K_X}(h_d) \end{equation} the moduli space of Gieseker semistable sheaves on $X$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ (with respect to the anticanonical polarization of $X$).
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: $\cM_d(X)$ parameterizes Gieseker semistable sheaves on $X$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d$ w.r.t. $-K_X$.

nodes.name: Closed points of the moduli spaces $\cM_d(X)$ for $d \in \{2,3,4\}$
nodes.statement: Let $\cF$ be a torsion free sheaf on $X$ whose Hilbert polynomial is $h_d(t)$ with $d \in \{2, 3, 4 \}$. $(i)$ If $d \in \{2, 3\}$ there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$ such that $\cF \cong \cE_z$. \newline $(ii)$ If $d \in \{3, 4\}$ there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_{6-d}$ such that $\cF \cong \cE_z^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: Every torsion-free sheaf with Hilbert polynomial $h_d$ is $\cE_z$ (for $d=2,3$) or $\cE_z^\vee\otimes\omega_X^{-1}$ (for $d=3,4$) for a unique $z$.
assumptions: Let $\cF$ be a torsion free sheaf on $X$ whose Hilbert polynomial is $h_d(t)$ with $d \in \{2, 3, 4 \}$.
conclusions: $(i)$ If $d \in \{2, 3\}$ there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$ such that $\cF \cong \cE_z$. \newline $(ii)$ If $d \in \{3, 4\}$ there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_{6-d}$ such that $\cF \cong \cE_z^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Fiberwise criteria for objects over a base scheme
nodes.statement: Assume $\cF \in \bD^-(M)$ and $M$ is proper over $S$, and in $(ii)$ and $(iii)$ that $M$ is flat over $S$. \begin{enumerate} \item[$(i)$] If $i_{M_s}^*(\cF) \in \bD^{\le p_0}(M_s)$ for some integer $p_0$ and all geometric points $s \in S$, then $\cF \in \bD^{\le p_0}(M)$. In particular, if $i_{M_s}^*(\cF) = 0$ for all geometric points $s \in S$, then $\cF = 0$. \item[$(ii)$] If for all geometric points $s \in S$ the pullback $i_{M_s}^*(\cF)$ is a pure sheaf such that $H^k(M_s, i_{M_s}^*\cF) = 0$ for all~$k \ne 0$ and $\dim H^0(M_s,i_{M_s}^*\cF) = r$ for a constant $r$, then $p_{S*}(\cF)$ is a vector bundle of rank~$r$ on~$S$. \item[$(iii)$] If for any geometric point $s \in S$ there is a point $m \in M_s$ such that $i_{M_s}^*(\cF) \cong \cO_m$, then there is a unique section $\varphi \colon S \to M$ of the projection $p_S$ and a line bundle $\cL \in \Pic(S)$ such that $\cF \cong \varphi_*\cL$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: Fiberwise amplitude, fiberwise cohomology and fiberwise structure-sheaf conditions propagate to the total space: vanishing, local freeness of $p_{S*}\cF$, and $\cF\cong\varphi_*\cL$ for a section $\varphi$.
assumptions: Assume $\cF \in \bD^-(M)$ and $M$ is proper over $S$, and in $(ii)$ and $(iii)$ that $M$ is flat over $S$.
conclusions: If $i_{M_s}^*(\cF) \in \bD^{\le p_0}(M_s)$ for some integer $p_0$ and all geometric points $s \in S$, then $\cF \in \bD^{\le p_0}(M)$. In particular, if $i_{M_s}^*(\cF) = 0$ for all geometric points $s \in S$, then $\cF = 0$. \item[$(ii)$] If for all geometric points $s \in S$ the pullback $i_{M_s}^*(\cF)$ is a pure sheaf such that $H^k(M_s, i_{M_s}^*\cF) = 0$ for all~$k \ne 0$ and $\dim H^0(M_s,i_{M_s}^*\cF) = r$ for a constant $r$, then $p_{S*}(\cF)$ is a vector bundle of rank~$r$ on~$S$. \item[$(iii)$] If for any geometric point $s \in S$ there is a point $m \in M_s$ such that $i_{M_s}^*(\cF) \cong \cO_m$, then there is a unique section $\varphi \colon S \to M$ of the projection $p_S$ and a line bundle $\cL \in \Pic(S)$ such that $\cF \cong \varphi_*\cL$.

nodes.name: Modular interpretation: $\cM_2(X)\cong\cM_4(X)\cong Z_2$ and $\cM_3(X)\cong Z_3$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field $\kk$. The moduli spaces $\cM_2(X)$, $\cM_3(X)$, and $\cM_4(X)$ are fine moduli spaces. Moreover, \newline$(i)$ $\cM_2(X) \cong \cM_4(X) \cong Z_2$ and the sheaves $\cE_{Z_2}$ and $\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are the corresponding universal families; \newline$(ii)$ $\cM_3(X) \cong Z_3$ and the sheaves $\cE_{Z_3}$ and $\cE_{Z_3}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are two universal families for this moduli problem.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: The moduli spaces of semistable sheaves with Hilbert polynomials $h_2,h_3,h_4$ are fine and are identified with $Z_2$, $Z_3$, $Z_2$, with universal families $\cE_{Z_d}$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field $\kk$.
conclusions: The moduli spaces $\cM_2(X)$, $\cM_3(X)$, and $\cM_4(X)$ are fine moduli spaces. Moreover, \newline$(i)$ $\cM_2(X) \cong \cM_4(X) \cong Z_2$ and the sheaves $\cE_{Z_2}$ and $\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are the corresponding universal families; \newline$(ii)$ $\cM_3(X) \cong Z_3$ and the sheaves $\cE_{Z_3}$ and $\cE_{Z_3}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are two universal families for this moduli problem.

nodes.name: An automorphism of $\cM_3(X)$ exchanging the two universal families
nodes.statement: There is an automorphism $\sigma \colon \cM_3(X) \to \cM_3(X)$ such that $\cE_{Z_3}^\vee \cong \sigma^*\cE_{Z_3} \otimes \omega_X$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
conclusions: There is an automorphism $\sigma \colon \cM_3(X) \to \cM_3(X)$ such that $\cE_{Z_3}^\vee \cong \sigma^*\cE_{Z_3} \otimes \omega_X$.

nodes.name: The polynomials $h'_d(t) = dt+1$
nodes.statement: Now consider the polynomial \begin{equation} h'_d(t) = dt + 1 \in \ZZ[t]. \end{equation} This is the Hilbert polynomial of a rational normal curve of degree $d$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation

nodes.name: Subschemes with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d$ are connected aCM curves
nodes.statement: Let $C \subset X \subset \P^6$ be a subscheme with Hilbert polynomial $h_C(t) = h'_d(t)$ and $1 \le d \le 3$. Then $C$ is a connected arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay curve.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
assumptions: Let $C \subset X \subset \P^6$ be a subscheme with Hilbert polynomial $h_C(t) = h'_d(t)$ and $1 \le d \le 3$.
conclusions: Then $C$ is a connected arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay curve.

nodes.name: Resolutions of $\cO_C$ for conics, twisted cubics and lines
nodes.statement: $(i)$ If $C \subset X$ is a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d(t)$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$ then there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to \cE_z^\vee \to \cO_X \to \cO_C \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism $\cE_z^\vee \to \cO_X$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to $\cO_C$. $(ii)$ Similarly, if $L \subset X$ is a line, i.e., a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_1(t)$ then there are unique closed points $z_2 \in Z_2$ and $z_3 \in Z_3$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to \cE_{z_2} \to \cE_{z_3} \to \cO_L \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism $\cE_{z_2} \to \cE_{z_3}$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to $\cO_L$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: Curves of degree $d\in\{2,3\}$ sit in $0\to\cE_z^\vee\to\cO_X\to\cO_C\to0$; lines sit in $0\to\cE_{z_2}\to\cE_{z_3}\to\cO_L\to0$.
assumptions: If $C \subset X$ is a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d(t)$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$
if $L \subset X$ is a line, i.e., a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_1(t)$
conclusions: then there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to \cE_z^\vee \to \cO_X \to \cO_C \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism $\cE_z^\vee \to \cO_X$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to $\cO_C$. $(ii)$ Similarly, if $L \subset X$ is a line, i.e., a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_1(t)$ then there are unique closed points $z_2 \in Z_2$ and $z_3 \in Z_3$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to \cE_{z_2} \to \cE_{z_3} \to \cO_L \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism $\cE_{z_2} \to \cE_{z_3}$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to $\cO_L$.

nodes.name: The Hilbert schemes $F_d(X)$
nodes.statement: Consider the Hilbert scheme \begin{equation} F_d(X) := \Hilb_{X,-K_X}(h'_d) \end{equation} of subschemes of $X$ with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d(t)$. Thus, $F_1(X)$ is the Hilbert scheme of lines, $F_2(X)$ is the Hilbert scheme of conics, and $F_3(X)$ is the Hilbert scheme of generalized twisted cubic curves on $X$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: $F_d(X)$ is the Hilbert scheme of subschemes of $X$ with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d$: lines, conics and twisted cubics for $d=1,2,3$.

nodes.name: Hilbert scheme interpretation of $Z_2$ and $Z_3$
nodes.statement: We have natural isomorphisms of Hilbert schemes \begin{equation*} F_1(X) \cong Z_2 \times Z_3, \qquad F_2(X) \cong \P_{Z_2}(p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}), \qquand F_3(X) \cong \P_{Z_3}(p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}). \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: $F_1(X)\cong Z_2\times Z_3$, while $F_2(X)$ and $F_3(X)$ are the projectivizations of $p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}$ and $p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}$.
assumptions: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} the sheaves $p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}$, $p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}$ and $p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*\cE_{Z_3})$ are locally free of ranks $2$, $3$ and $1$ on $Z_2$, $Z_3$ and~$Z_2 \times Z_3$ respectively.
conclusions: We have natural isomorphisms of Hilbert schemes \begin{equation*} F_1(X) \cong Z_2 \times Z_3, \qquad F_2(X) \cong \P_{Z_2}(p_{2*}\cE_{Z_2}), \qquand F_3(X) \cong \P_{Z_3}(p_{3*}\cE_{Z_3}).

nodes.name: The Hilbert scheme $F_4(X)$
nodes.statement: With the same argument one can prove that $p_{2*}(\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1})$ is a rank-4 vector bundle on~$Z_2$ and that~$F_4(X) \cong \P_{Z_2}(p_{2*}(\cE_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}))$.
nodes.section: 4 Moduli spaces interpretation
nodes.statement_short: $F_4(X)$ is the projectivization of the rank-4 bundle $p_{2*}(\cE_{Z_2}^\vee\otimes\omega_X^{-1})$ on $Z_2$.

nodes.name: Algebraically closed base field in Sections 2--4
nodes.statement: In this section $\kk$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic distinct from~2 and~3.
nodes.section: 2 Preliminaries

nodes.name: Arbitrary base field from Section 5 onwards
nodes.statement: Starting from this section we assume that $\kk$ is an arbitrary field of characteristic distinct from~2 and~3, unless something else is specified explicitly. We keep in mind the notation introduced in previous sections.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces

nodes.name: du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement: A family $f \colon \cX \to S$ is a {\sf du Val family} of sextic del Pezzo surfaces, if $f$ is a flat projective morphism such that for every geometric point $s \in S$ the fiber $\cX_s$ of $\cX$ over $s$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface (Definition~\ref{definition:dp6}), i.e., a normal integral surface with at worst du Val singularities such that $-K_{\cX_s}$ is an ample Cartier divisor and $K_{\cX_s}^2 = 6$.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
differentia: for every geometric point $s \in S$ the fiber $\cX_s$ of $\cX$ over $s$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface

nodes.name: du Val families form a stack and have invertible relative dualizing sheaf
nodes.statement: Note also that by definition all fibers of $f \colon \cX \to S$ are Gorenstein, hence the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{\cX/S}^\bullet$ when restricted to any fiber of $f$ is an invertible sheaf, hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is an invertible sheaf on the total space $\cX$. If $f \colon \cX \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces then for any base change $S' \to S$ the induced family $f' \colon \cX' = \cX \times_S S' \to S'$ is still a du Val family. So, du Val families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces form a stack over $(\mathrm{Sch}/\kk)$.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: All fibers are Gorenstein so $\omega_{\cX/S}^\bullet$ is invertible, and du Val families are stable under base change, hence form a stack.
conclusions: Note also that by definition all fibers of $f \colon \cX \to S$ are Gorenstein, hence the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{\cX/S}^\bullet$ when restricted to any fiber of $f$ is an invertible sheaf, hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is an invertible sheaf on the total space $\cX$.
So, du Val families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces form a stack over $(\mathrm{Sch}/\kk)$.

nodes.name: Main theorem: semiorthogonal decomposition for a du Val family
nodes.statement: Assume $f \colon \cX \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. Then there is an~$S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition \textup{(}compatible with any base change\textup{)} \begin{equation} \bD(\cX) = \langle \bD(S), \bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2}), \bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3}) \rangle, \end{equation} where $\cZ_2 \to S$ and $\cZ_3 \to S$ are finite flat morphisms of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively, $\beta_{\cZ_2}$ and $\beta_{\cZ_3}$ are Brauer classes of order $2$ and $3$ respectively on them, and the last two components are the twisted derived categories.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: For any du Val family $\cX\to S$, $\bD(\cX)=\langle\bD(S),\bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2}),\bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})\rangle$ with finite flat $\cZ_d\to S$ of degrees $3,2$.
assumptions: Assume $f \colon \cX \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces.
conclusions: Then there is an~$S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition \textup{(}compatible with any base change\textup{)} \begin{equation} \bD(\cX) = \langle \bD(S), \bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2}), \bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3}) \rangle, \end{equation} where $\cZ_2 \to S$ and $\cZ_3 \to S$ are finite flat morphisms of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively, $\beta_{\cZ_2}$ and $\beta_{\cZ_3}$ are Brauer classes of order $2$ and $3$ respectively on them, and the last two components are the twisted derived categories.

nodes.name: The relative moduli stacks $\cM_d(\cX/S)$
nodes.statement: Let $f \colon \cX \to S$ be a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. For $d \in \{2,3,4\}$ let $\cM_d(\cX/S)$ denote the relative moduli stack of semistable sheaves on fibers of $\cX$ over $S$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ defined in~\eqref{eq:hd}.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces

nodes.name: $\cM_d(\cX/S)$ is a $\Gm$-gerbe over $\cZ_d(\cX/S)$
nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3,4\}$ the stack $\cM_d(\cX/S)$ is a $\Gm$-gerbe over its coarse module space \begin{equation*} \cZ_d(\cX/S) := (\cM_d(\cX/S))_{\mathrm{coarse}} \end{equation*} with an obstruction given by a Brauer class $\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX/S)}$ of order \begin{equation} \operatorname{ord} \beta_{\cZ_d(\cX/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Moreover, there is an isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces $\sigma_{2,4} \colon \cZ_4(\cX/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \cZ_2(\cX/S)$ and an automorphism $\sigma_{3,3} \colon \cZ_3(\cX/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \cZ_3(\cX/S)$, such that \begin{equation*} \beta_{\cZ_4(\cX/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{\cZ_2(\cX/S)}^{-1}) = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{\cZ_2(\cX/S)}) \qquand \beta_{\cZ_3(\cX/S)} = \sigma_{3,3}^*(\beta_{\cZ_3(\cX/S)}^{-1}). \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: The relative moduli stack is a $\Gm$-gerbe over its coarse space with Brauer obstruction of order $2$ ($d=2,4$) or $3$ ($d=3$), and $\cZ_4\cong\cZ_2$.
conclusions: the stack $\cM_d(\cX/S)$ is a $\Gm$-gerbe over its coarse module space \begin{equation*} \cZ_d(\cX/S) := (\cM_d(\cX/S))_{\mathrm{coarse}} \end{equation*} with an obstruction given by a Brauer class $\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX/S)}$ of order \begin{equation} \operatorname{ord} \beta_{\cZ_d(\cX/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Moreover, there is an isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces $\sigma_{2,4} \colon \cZ_4(\cX/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \cZ_2(\cX/S)$ and an automorphism $\sigma_{3,3} \colon \cZ_3(\cX/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \cZ_3(\cX/S)$, such that \begin{equation*} \beta_{\cZ_4(\cX/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{\cZ_2(\cX/S)}^{-1}) = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{\cZ_2(\cX/S)}) \qquand \beta_{\cZ_3(\cX/S)} = \sigma_{3,3}^*(\beta_{\cZ_3(\cX/S)}^{-1}).

nodes.name: Base change compatibility of $\cM_d$, $\cZ_d$ and the universal families
nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon S' \to S$ be a base change and denote $\cX' := \cX \times_S S'$. We have \begin{equation} \cM_d(\cX'/S') \cong \cM_d(\cX/S) \times_S S' \qquand \cZ_d(\cX'/S') \cong \cZ_d(\cX/S) \times_S S'. \end{equation} Moreover, isomorphisms~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} are compatible with the universal families, i.e., \begin{equation} \beta_{\cZ'_d} = \phi_{\cZ_d}^*(\beta_{\cZ_d}) \qquand \cE_{\cZ'_d} \cong \phi_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d}^*\cE_{\cZ_d}. \end{equation} where we set $\cZ'_d := \cZ_d(\cX'/S')$ and denote the morphisms induced by the base change by $\phi_\cX \colon \cX' \to \cX$, $\phi_{\cZ_d} \colon \cZ'_d \to \cZ_d$, and $\phi_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d} \colon \cX' \times_{S'} \cZ'_d \to \cX \times_S \cZ_d$, respectively.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: Both the moduli stack and its coarse space commute with base change, compatibly with Brauer classes and universal families.
assumptions: Let $\phi \colon S' \to S$ be a base change and denote $\cX' := \cX \times_S S'$.
conclusions: We have \begin{equation} \cM_d(\cX'/S') \cong \cM_d(\cX/S) \times_S S' \qquand \cZ_d(\cX'/S') \cong \cZ_d(\cX/S) \times_S S'. \end{equation} Moreover, isomorphisms~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} are compatible with the universal families, i.e., \begin{equation} \beta_{\cZ'_d} = \phi_{\cZ_d}^*(\beta_{\cZ_d}) \qquand \cE_{\cZ'_d} \cong \phi_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d}^*\cE_{\cZ_d}.

nodes.name: Geometric fibers of $\cM_d(\cX/S)$ and $\cZ_d(\cX/S)$
nodes.statement: For any geometric point $s \in S$ there are isomorphisms \begin{equation} \cM_d(\cX/S)_s \cong \cM_d(X), \qquad \cZ_d(\cX/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquand i_{Z_d}^*(\cE_{\cZ_d}) \cong \cE_{Z_d}, \end{equation} where $X = \cX_s$ is the fiber of $\cX$ over $s$ and $i_{Z_d} \colon Z_d \cong \cZ_d(\cX/S)_s \hookrightarrow \cZ_d(\cX/S)$ is the natural embedding.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: Over a geometric point $s$ the relative moduli space and coarse space specialize to $\cM_d(X)$ and $Z_d$ of the fiber $X=\cX_s$.
assumptions: For any geometric point $s \in S$
conclusions: there are isomorphisms \begin{equation} \cM_d(\cX/S)_s \cong \cM_d(X), \qquad \cZ_d(\cX/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquand i_{Z_d}^*(\cE_{\cZ_d}) \cong \cE_{Z_d}, \end{equation} where $X = \cX_s$ is the fiber of $\cX$ over $s$ and $i_{Z_d} \colon Z_d \cong \cZ_d(\cX/S)_s \hookrightarrow \cZ_d(\cX/S)$ is the natural embedding.

nodes.name: $\cZ_2 \to S$ and $\cZ_3 \to S$ are finite flat of degrees $3$ and $2$
nodes.statement: The maps $f_2 \colon \cZ_2 \to S$ and $f_3 \colon \cZ_3 \to S$ are finite flat maps of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively. The relative dualizing complexes $\omega_{\cZ_2/S}^\bullet$ and $\omega_{\cZ_3/S}^\bullet$ are line bundles.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
assumptions: When there is no risk of confusion, we abbreviate $\cM_d(\cX/S)$ and $\cZ_d(\cX/S)$ to $\cM_d$ and $\cZ_d$. Both the stack $\cM_d$ and the scheme $\cZ_d$ are proper over $S$. We denote by \begin{equation*} f_d \colon \cZ_d \to S \end{equation*} the natural projection.
conclusions: The maps $f_2 \colon \cZ_2 \to S$ and $f_3 \colon \cZ_3 \to S$ are finite flat maps of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively.
The relative dualizing complexes $\omega_{\cZ_2/S}^\bullet$ and $\omega_{\cZ_3/S}^\bullet$ are line bundles.

nodes.name: Flatness and finite $\Ext$-amplitude of $\cE_{\cZ_d}$
nodes.statement: For each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ the sheaf $\cE_{\cZ_d}$ is flat over $\cZ_d$ and has finite $\Ext$-amplitude over $\cX$.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
assumptions: For each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$
conclusions: the sheaf $\cE_{\cZ_d}$ is flat over $\cZ_d$ and has finite $\Ext$-amplitude over $\cX$.

nodes.name: The Fourier--Mukai functors $\Phi_d$
nodes.statement: For each~$d \in \{1,2,3\}$ we consider the Fourier--Mukai functor whose kernel is the universal family $\cE_{\cZ_d}$, considered as a $\beta_{\cZ_d}^{-1}$-twisted sheaf on $\cX \times_S \cZ_d$: \begin{equation} \Phi_d = \Phi_{\cE_{\cZ_d}} := p_*(\cE_{\cZ_d} \otimes p_d^*(-)) \colon \bD(\cZ_d,\beta_{\cZ_d}) \to \bD(\cX). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_d = p_*(\cE_{\cZ_d}\otimes p_d^*(-))$ embeds the twisted derived category $\bD(\cZ_d,\beta_{\cZ_d})$ into $\bD(\cX)$.

nodes.name: $S$-linearity and right adjoint of $\Phi_d$
nodes.statement: The functor $\Phi_d$ is $S$-linear, preserves boundedness and perfectness, and its right adjoint functor is \begin{equation} \Phi_d^! \colon \bD(\cX) \to \bD(\cZ_d,\beta_{\cZ_d}),\qquad \Phi_d^!(\cG) \cong p_{d*}\RCHom(\cE_{\cZ_d},p^!\cG). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_d$ is $S$-linear, preserves boundedness and perfectness, and $\Phi_d^!(\cG)=p_{d*}\RCHom(\cE_{\cZ_d},p^!\cG)$.
conclusions: The functor $\Phi_d$ is $S$-linear, preserves boundedness and perfectness, and its right adjoint functor is \begin{equation} \Phi_d^! \colon \bD(\cX) \to \bD(\cZ_d,\beta_{\cZ_d}),\qquad \Phi_d^!(\cG) \cong p_{d*}\RCHom(\cE_{\cZ_d},p^!\cG).

nodes.name: Fourier--Mukai form of $\Phi_d^!$ and its base change compatibility
nodes.statement: We have an isomorphism of functors \begin{equation*} \Phi_d^!(\cG) \cong p_{d*}(\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S} \otimes p^*(\cG)), \end{equation*} where $\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee := \RCHom(\cE_{\cZ_d},\cO_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d})$ is a coherent sheaf flat over $\cZ_d$. The kernel~$\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S}$ of this functor is compativle with base changes, i.e., if $\phi \colon S' \to S$ is a base change, then \begin{equation*} \phi_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d}^*(\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S}) \cong \cE_{\cZ'_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^{\prime*}\omega_{\cZ'_d/S'}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_d^!$ is the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee\otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S}$, compatible with base change.
conclusions: We have an isomorphism of functors \begin{equation*} \Phi_d^!(\cG) \cong p_{d*}(\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S} \otimes p^*(\cG)), \end{equation*} where $\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee := \RCHom(\cE_{\cZ_d},\cO_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d})$ is a coherent sheaf flat over $\cZ_d$. The kernel~$\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S}$ of this functor is compativle with base changes, i.e., if $\phi \colon S' \to S$ is a base change, then \begin{equation*} \phi_{\cX \times_S \cZ_d}^*(\cE_{\cZ_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{\cZ_d/S}) \cong \cE_{\cZ'_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^{\prime*}\omega_{\cZ'_d/S'}.

nodes.name: $S$-linearity and base change compatibility of $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$
nodes.statement: The functors $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$ are $S$-linear and compatible with base changes, i.e., \begin{align*} \Phi'_d \circ \phi_{\cZ_d}^* &\cong \phi_{\cX}^* \circ \Phi_d, & \phi_{\cX*} \circ \Phi'_d &\cong \Phi_d \circ \phi_{\cZ_d*}, \\ \Phi^{\prime!}_d \circ \phi_{\cX}^* &\cong \phi_{\cZ_d}^* \circ \Phi_d^!, & \phi_{\cZ_d*} \circ \Phi^{\prime!}_d &\cong \Phi_d^! \circ \phi_{\cX*}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
conclusions: The functors $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$ are $S$-linear and compatible with base changes, i.e., \begin{align*} \Phi'_d \circ \phi_{\cZ_d}^* &\cong \phi_{\cX}^* \circ \Phi_d, & \phi_{\cX*} \circ \Phi'_d &\cong \Phi_d \circ \phi_{\cZ_d*}, \\ \Phi^{\prime!}_d \circ \phi_{\cX}^* &\cong \phi_{\cZ_d}^* \circ \Phi_d^!, & \phi_{\cZ_d*} \circ \Phi^{\prime!}_d &\cong \Phi_d^! \circ \phi_{\cX*}.

nodes.name: Admissibility, finite amplitude and the perfect version of the decomposition
nodes.statement: The components of the semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible and their projection functors have finite cohomological amplitude. Moreover, the functors $\Phi_d$ preserve perfectness and induce a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(\cX) = \langle \Phi_1(\bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(S)), \Phi_2(\bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2})), \Phi_3(\bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})) \rangle. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: The components are admissible with finite-amplitude projections, and the decomposition restricts to perfect complexes.
conclusions: The components of the semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible and their projection functors have finite cohomological amplitude. Moreover, the functors $\Phi_d$ preserve perfectness and induce a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(\cX) = \langle \Phi_1(\bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(S)), \Phi_2(\bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2})), \Phi_3(\bD^{\mathrm{perf}}(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})) \rangle.

nodes.name: The relative duality functor $\rD_{\cX/S}$
nodes.statement: Since the morphism $f \colon \cX \to S$ is Gorenstein, the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{\cX/S}$ is (up to a shift) a line bundle. Therefore, the relative duality functor \begin{equation*} \rD_{\cX/S}(\cF) := \RCHom(\cF , f^*\omega_S^\bullet) \end{equation*} is an anti-autoequivalence of the category $\bD(\cX)$ (see Section~\ref{subsection:duality}).
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces

nodes.name: Relative-duality-dual semiorthogonal decomposition
nodes.statement: The relative duality functor gives a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(\cX) = \langle \rD_{\cX/S}(\bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})), \rD_{\cX/S}(\bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2})), \rD_{\cX/S}(\bD(S)) \rangle, \end{equation} whose components are equivalent to $\bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})$, $\bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2})$, and $\bD(S)$ respectively. Moreover, this decomposition is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6}.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: $\rD_{\cX/S}$ produces the right mutation-dual decomposition with the same three component categories.
assumptions: Since the morphism $f \colon \cX \to S$ is Gorenstein, the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{\cX/S}$ is (up to a shift) a line bundle. Therefore, the relative duality functor \begin{equation*} \rD_{\cX/S}(\cF) := \RCHom(\cF , f^*\omega_S^\bullet) \end{equation*} is an anti-autoequivalence of the category $\bD(\cX)$
conclusions: The relative duality functor gives a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} \bD(\cX) = \langle \rD_{\cX/S}(\bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})), \rD_{\cX/S}(\bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2})), \rD_{\cX/S}(\bD(S)) \rangle, \end{equation} whose components are equivalent to $\bD(\cZ_3,\beta_{\cZ_3})$, $\bD(\cZ_2,\beta_{\cZ_2})$, and $\bD(S)$ respectively. Moreover, this decomposition is right mutation-dual to~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6}.

nodes.name: Regularity criterion for the total space of the family
nodes.statement: Let $\cX \to S$ be a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. The total space $\cX$ of the family is regular if and only if all three schemes $S$, $\cZ_2$ and $\cZ_3$ are regular.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
assumptions: Let $\cX \to S$ be a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces.
conclusions: The total space $\cX$ of the family is regular if and only if all three schemes $S$, $\cZ_2$ and $\cZ_3$ are regular.

nodes.name: Smoothness of $\cX \to S$ versus smoothness of $\cZ_d \to S$
nodes.statement: Note also that a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces $\cX \to S$ is smooth over $S$ if and only if the maps $\cZ_2 \to S$ and $\cZ_3 \to S$ are smooth (i.e.\ unramified). Indeed, this follows from Corollary~\ref{corollary:S-s} and the description of the fibers~$Z_d$ of $\cZ_d \to S$ in Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: $\cX\to S$ is smooth exactly when $\cZ_2\to S$ and $\cZ_3\to S$ are unramified.

nodes.name: Extension of an $S_0$-isomorphism of the schemes $\cZ_d$
nodes.statement: Let $\cX \to S$ and $\cX' \to S$ be two du Val families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces with regular total spaces $\cX$ and $\cX'$. Assume there is a dense open subset $S_0 \subset S$ such that for some $d \in \{2,3\}$ there is an $S_0$-isomorphism $\varphi_0 \colon \cZ_d(\cX_0/S_0) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\cZ_d(\cX'_0/S_0)$, where $\cX_0 = \cX \times_S S_0$ and~$\cX'_0 = \cX' \times_S S_0$. Then~$\varphi_0$ extends to an isomorphism $\varphi \colon \cZ_d(\cX/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \cZ_d(\cX'/S)$ over $S$. Moreover, if we have an equality of Brauer classes $\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX_0/S_0)} = \varphi_0^*\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX'_0/S_0)}$ then it extends to $\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX/S)} = \varphi^*\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX'/S)}$.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: For regular total spaces, an isomorphism of the $\cZ_d$ over a dense open $S_0$ extends over $S$, together with the Brauer classes.
assumptions: Let $\cX \to S$ and $\cX' \to S$ be two du Val families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces with regular total spaces $\cX$ and $\cX'$. Assume there is a dense open subset $S_0 \subset S$ such that for some $d \in \{2,3\}$ there is an $S_0$-isomorphism $\varphi_0 \colon \cZ_d(\cX_0/S_0) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\cZ_d(\cX'_0/S_0)$, where $\cX_0 = \cX \times_S S_0$ and~$\cX'_0 = \cX' \times_S S_0$.
conclusions: Then~$\varphi_0$ extends to an isomorphism $\varphi \colon \cZ_d(\cX/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \cZ_d(\cX'/S)$ over $S$. Moreover, if we have an equality of Brauer classes $\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX_0/S_0)} = \varphi_0^*\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX'_0/S_0)}$ then it extends to $\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX/S)} = \varphi^*\beta_{\cZ_d(\cX'/S)}$.

nodes.name: Relative Hilbert schemes as Severi--Brauer varieties over $\cZ_2$, $\cZ_3$
nodes.statement: For each $1 \le d \le 3$ the scheme $F_d(\cX/S)$ is flat over $S$, and \begin{itemize} \item $F_1(\cX/S) \cong \cZ_2 \times_S \cZ_3$, \item $F_2(\cX/S)$ is an \'etale locally trivial $\P^1$-bundle over $\cZ_2$, and \item $F_3(\cX/S)$ is an \'etale locally trivial $\P^2$-bundle over $\cZ_3$. \end{itemize} Moreover, $F_2(\cX/S)$ and $F_3(\cX/S)$ are Severi--Brauer varieties over~$\cZ_2$ and~$\cZ_3$ associated with the Brauer classes $\beta_{\cZ_2}$ and $\beta_{\cZ_3}$, respectively.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: $F_1(\cX/S)\cong\cZ_2\times_S\cZ_3$, and $F_2,F_3$ are étale locally trivial $\P^1$- and $\P^2$-bundles realizing the Brauer classes.
assumptions: For each $1 \le d \le 3$
